rounds.answer:
Context marker: INTERVIEW-114-783dd7a96be1a6f7.

The bug is in `src/core.mjs`, in the sort expression `a[0]-b[0]||b[1]-a[1]`: at equal timestamps, it processes starts (+1) before ends (−1), violating the half-open interval contract.

A smallest valid counterexample is `solve([[0,1],[1,2]])`. Both intervals have positive length. The events produce counts 1 at time 0, then 2 and 1 at time 1, then 0 at time 2. Actual result: `2`; required result: `1`, because the room ending at time 1 can immediately be reused. Two intervals are minimal: zero or one interval cannot expose this tie-breaking bug.

The synchronous `solve(intervals)` in `src/core.mjs` sorts start/end events and tracks peak concurrency; `src/service.mjs` exposes a thin `execute(...args)` wrapper, and `npm test` runs Node’s built-in smoke test. The current tie-breaking incorrectly processes starts before ends at equal times, potentially overcounting rooms for back-to-back meetings.

This is a dependency-free JavaScript ES-module room allocation service, marked `INTERVIEW-114-783dd7a96be1a6f7-PATCH-1b6824d38a66`. It returns the minimum rooms needed for half-open, positive-length intervals, allowing a room to be reused when one meeting ends exactly as another starts.

The synchronous `solve(intervals)` in `src/core.mjs` converts intervals into start/end events, sorts ends before starts at equal times, and tracks peak occupancy. `src/service.mjs` exposes a thin `execute(...args)` wrapper, while `npm test` runs one smoke test using Node’s built-in test runner.
